correctness.rationale: For a fixed leak, extra blue vertices cannot hinder closure. With a blue hub, start from a rim adjacent pair: the two fronts of the remaining white interval cannot both be disabled by one leak, and if one reaches an initially white leak the other finishes the rest. Without a pair no force can start, including from the hub. With a white hub the only possible first move targets the hub, from a selected triple center; exactly two or more candidate centers survive arbitrary deletion of a force source. The trace counts labelled cyclic words, with one factor z per selected bit and one u per cyclic 111; expanding the determinant gives the stated constant and linear terms in u, and the logarithmic derivative extracts the ordinary generating function. Minimal hub-free sets are four-blocks or two three-blocks with both gaps nonempty; overlapping one-bit windows contain a redundant four-block. At n=4 all four-block descriptions give one rim set. At n>=8 the second block has n-7 allowed offsets, and unordered pairs divide by two. Independent fort-transversal enumeration exhaustively checks the criterion and minimal counts through n=14; it is a supplement to the all-n proof, not extrapolation.
residual_risks: The proof is for ordinary forcing with exactly one disabled source and labelled rim length n>=4; it does not use or cover PSD forcing, multiple leaks, or unlabeled necklaces.
